text:
Predicates:
SpillsFood(x) ::: x spills a lot of food on his clothing.
Tidy(x) ::: x is notably tidy.
ClumsyFoodie(x) ::: x is a clumsy foodie.
GoesOutFrequent(x) ::: x goes out frequently to find new food restaurants.
Cleanly(x) ::: x is cleanly.
ValuOrderSpotless(x) ::: x values order and spotlessness.
FamilyPrioritizeOrderSpotless(x) ::: x's family prioritizes order and spotlessness.
ValueOrderSpotless(x) ::: x values order and spotlessness.
Peter(x) ::: x is Peter.
Premises:
∀x (SpillsFood(x) → ¬Tidy(x)) ::: If people spill a lot of food on their clothing, then they are not notably tidy.
∀x (ClumsyFoodie(x) ∧ GoesOutFrequent(x) → SpillsFood(x)) ::: All clumsy foodies who go out frequently spill food.
∀x (Cleanly(x) → Tidy(x)) ::: If people are cleanly, then they are notably tidy.
∀x (ValuOrderSpotless(x) → Cleanly(x)) ::: If people value order and spotlessness, then they are cleanly.
∀x (FamilyPrioritizeOrderSpotless(x) → ValueOrderSpotless(x)) ::: All people whose families prioritize order and spotlessness value order and spotlessness.
Peter(x) ::: Peter is a person.
Premises:
(SpillsFood(Peter) ∧ Cleanly(Peter)) ∨ (¬SpillsFood(Peter) ∧ ¬Cleanly(Peter)) ::: Peter is either a person who spills food and is cleanly, or does not spill food and is not cleanly.
Conclusion:
¬Tidy(Peter) ::: Peter is not notably tidy.
